newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan lends for financial centre, shopping mall.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan lends for financial centre, shopping mall.

text.p: A Taiwan cabinet agency said on Tuesday it would lend T$14.2 billion to finance a state-backed international financial centre in Taipei and T$11.921 billion for a major private shopping mall, also in the capital.
The Council for Economic Planning and Development said the loan for the Taipei International Financial Centre would have a 20-year term, with an option to extend another five years.
The lending rate would float at the equivalent of the one-year post-office deposit rate plus one percentage point. The current one-year postal rate is 6.2 percent.

Taipei's municipal government already has set aside prime downtown land for the T$24 billion financial centre project and will select contractors through open bidding, an official of the cabinet council said by telephone.

The T$11.921 billion loan will help finance a T$23.96 billion private shopping mall to be built in downtown Taipei by a consortium led by Core Pacific Group, a private group with intimate business links to the ruling Nationalist Party.
The consortium is led by two Core Pacific allies, BES Engineering and China Petrochemical, and Nationalist Party-controlled China Development.
Singapore investors hold a 10 percent stake in the project and Japanese partners one percent, the official said.
